Operating model

Make the operating
model explicit.

Connect purpose, decision rights, delivery and evidence. The hive metaphor explains how the parts cooperate; familiar business terms come first.

THE WHOLE MODEL

Four connected views. One operating practice.

01⬡

Common baseline

Ownership, agreement, classification, authorised access and auditability.

02≋

Five operating layers

THE WHOLE MODEL

Five layers. One traceable thread.

Follow a decision from intent to evidence. Each layer gives the next one something concrete to work with.

Four connected views. One operating practice.

Every shared product needs ownership, a contract, a classification, policy-based access and an audit trail. Each ecosystem adapts role names, approval routes, thresholds and review cadences around that minimum.

BIO-INSPIRED BY DESIGN

Different roles.
A shared ecosystem.

Hives and beekeeping give us a language for cooperation, local responsibility and care for the whole. It is an organisational metaphor: people, decision rights and data products remain explicit.

The metaphor helps explain the model. It does not replace an organisation’s terminology or assign human roles based on bee biology.

EcosystemShared purpose+

The boundary of collaboration: objectives, participating domains, common policies and accountable governance. Start with a use case and a named sponsor.

Typical evidence

Policy, decision log, value indicator

Business domainHive+

A domain with an accountable owner, its own meaning and priorities. It coordinates its Cells while respecting the ecosystem’s minimum rules.

Typical evidence

Domain charter, owner, glossary

Business subdomainCell+

A focused subdomain inside a Hive. Stewardship and engineering work close to the data. A Cell can own several data products; the Cell is not itself a product.

Typical evidence

Steward, quality rules, product inventory

Business groupingComb · optional+

An optional grouping of Cells within the same Hive. A Cell may belong to several Combs. This is a business and permission grouping, not an extra infrastructure layer.

Typical evidence

Grouping criteria, scoped responsibilities

Data productAccountable offering+

A purposeful offering with a named owner, versioned contract, known consumers, quality expectations and a lifecycle. Tables, APIs and dashboards can be delivery interfaces.

Typical evidence

Contract, tests, access record, usage

Execution environmentFarm+

Where products are cultivated and operated: production, test or development environments. The Farm is an execution boundary, distinct from business ownership.

Typical evidence

Inventory, access controls, recovery evidence

01 / Operating model

Roles describe accountability.
Interfaces support the work.

A person may hold several roles. Record the role exercised for each decision. Consumer, Producer, EcOps and PlatOps are product interaction perspectives, not substitutes for business accountability.

RoleScopeResponsibilityReference interface
Governance forumEcosystemSets the baseline, reviews cross-domain exceptions and resolves conflicts.EcOps records decisions
Ecosystem managerEcosystemCoordinates implementation, scope, policy versions and improvement follow-up.EcOps
Domain ownerHiveAccountable for the domain and escalated approval decisions.EcOps / Producer
Subdomain ownerCellAccountable for the subdomain and its approval decisions.Producer
Data product ownerProductOwns purpose, contract, versions, publication and consumer relationships.Producer
Operational stewardCell; optionally HiveMaintains meaning, classification and quality; reviews requests.Producer / EcOps
Coordinating stewardHiveCoordinates stewardship and resolves issues across Cells.EcOps
Data engineeringCell; optionally HiveBuilds and maintains reproducible data preparation and delivery.Producer
Technical custodianFarmOperates environments and implements authorised controls.PlatOps / EcOps
ConsumerProductUses data within agreed terms and provides feedback on fitness for purpose.Consumer

When no subdomain owner is assigned, make the domain owner’s inherited responsibility explicit. A Comb may group permissions without creating a new role. Exact segregation of duties depends on risk and context.

DAMA-DMBOK 2 / DCAM / DATA MESH

Three lenses, with clear boundaries.

ReferenceWhat KDV operationalisesWhat still needs its own work
DAMA-DMBOK 2 · Revised EditionOwnership, metadata, quality, security and lifecycle working practices.Architecture, modelling, master data, integration, storage and other disciplines need context-specific design and specialist work.
DCAM · v3 reference lensCapability improvement supported by engagement, process and evidence.A technical event count is not a capability assessment. Use the publisher’s licensed assessment method when that is the objective.
Data Mesh · four principlesDomain ownership, data as a product, self-service and federated governance.Organisational boundaries, platform capability and viable product funding must be designed; terminology alone does not create a data mesh.

IMPLEMENTATION CHOICES

Apply the method with the tools that fit.

The operating model stays the same. Automation and hosting choices depend on scale, skills, risk and existing architecture.

01

Start with a small team

Documents, a controlled spreadsheet and a review meeting can establish ownership, agreements and decisions.

Suitable for a bounded first case; manually verify access and evidence.

02

Use your existing platform

Connect the method to your catalogue, identity provider, data platform and service management.

Prefer interoperable interfaces, explicit exit paths and recoverable evidence.

03

Use a reference implementation

Combine selected open-source tools or optional KDV implementations where they fit the requirements.

Verify each component’s version, licence, support, availability and operating responsibilities.

IMPLEMENTATION CHOICES

A reference architecture, not a mandatory stack.

01

Consumers

Applications · analytics · authorised AI use

02

Product interfaces

Contracts · catalogue · quality · access decisions

03

Reusable controls

Identity · policy enforcement · lineage · audit

04

Data execution

Existing databases · lakehouse · pipelines · recovery

Business domains organise accountability. Execution environments organise operation. Data sovereignty also involves control, authority, contracts, jurisdiction and portability.

Illustrative open-source options: OpenMetadata, Keycloak, Apache Ranger, OpenLineage, Airflow, dbt Core, Trino, Apache Iceberg and Superset. Selection is contextual; these names do not describe a validated integrated distribution.

AI / IA / LGPD / GDPR

Prepare data for AI with explicit use boundaries.

A catalogue entry or an AI connector is not sufficient. Apply governance to the intended use, inputs, outputs and human decisions.

01

Purpose and authority

Identify the intended use and who may authorise it; a new AI use may need a new decision.

02

Minimisation and access

Limit data and privileges to what that purpose needs, including retrieval and derived outputs.

03

Provenance and evaluation

Record source, freshness and limitations; evaluate answer quality and monitor harmful failures.

04

People and rights

Plan review, contestability, incident handling and the exercise of applicable rights.
